term: superabundant perfection, per-se necessity and differentiation cases in SCG I42
definition: The chapter distinguishes necessary-through-itself beings from caused necessities, a common notion from numerical identity, and accidental versus necessity-completing distinction. The accidental branch invokes essence-or-external causation; the completing branch distinguishes included nature from actual specification. Divine-nature multiplication additionally excludes essential differences, accidents and matter.
note: These are source argument commitments, not a formal case-exhaustion theorem or identity with the existing HasLimitingPrinciple disjunction. Application to the same root, addition-excluding esse, causal-ground correspondence and formal/eminent perfection remain open. No common predicate implies one object by definition.
